parsed.why: No trans criminalisation; courts grant recognition; but 2024 reports of street and institutional discrimination, physical/sexual harassment of visibly trans people, and rising political hate speech and threats. Recourse exists but is slow and partial.

Morality law criminalises all extra-marital sex; presidential decree frames LGBTQ as national-defence threat; mob attacks on trans women, venue raids, and a trans traveller's death in custody. Organised targeting with state framing.

No criminalisation, gender-marker documents issued without surgery, acceptance polling rising to 70%. But hate-crime law omits gender identity, violence reporting is dated (2012), and martial-law border checks screen male markers.

No criminalisation or visitor-facing restriction, but ombudsperson found police failed to protect LGBT assembly and hate-crime victim support is systemically lacking; large street protests; courts nonetheless uphold expression and partnership.

Never criminalised, visible scene, cooperative government posture, but documented police targeting of trans women (extortion, forced bathing) and 135+ harassment cases with no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse.
